title: News and misinformation consumption: A temporal comparison across European countries
screen_reason: Analysis of all tweets posted by NewsGuard-rated news outlet accounts in France, Germany, Italy and the UK from 1 January 2019 to 11 November 2021 (25.1 million tweets). Table 2 gives, per country, the total number of tweets and the number posted by questionable outlets (NewsGuard trust score below 60), which yields the share of news-outlet output coming from untrustworthy sources. That is a CONTENT share: the denominator is everything the rated outlets published.

estimates.measure_type: % of tweets posted by French news outlets that came from a NewsGuard-questionable outlet
estimates.value_raw: 932,105 questionable tweets / 7,083,659 total tweets (6,151,554 reliable + 932,105 questionable) = 13.16%
estimates.denominator: 7,083,659 tweets posted by the 236 France-based news outlets rated by NewsGuard (187 reliable, 49 questionable)
estimates.definition: The tweet was posted by a news outlet whose NewsGuard trust score is below 60 ('questionable')
estimates.misinfo_def: "News sources are categorized into two groups based on their score: Reliable (trust score greater or equal to 60) and Questionable (trust score less than 60)."
estimates.ground_truth_detail: NewsGuard trust scores (0-100) assigned by professional independent journalists on nine journalistic criteria, consistent across the four countries; coverage represents at least 90% of engagement in each country
estimates.moderator_quote: The dataset included all the tweets published by the selected accounts in the period from 01 January 2019 to 11 November 2021, resulting in 25+ Million tweets.
estimates.notes: Value computed as an exact part/whole from the verbatim counts in Table 2 (reliable + questionable sum exactly to the country total). The percentages printed in Table 2's parentheses are each country's contribution to the column totals, not the questionable share. Unit of the denominator is the news outlets' own output, so this is CONTENT rather than exposure or sharing; population_scope is 'other' because the actors are media organisations. Year set to the end of the collection window.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted: (a) the four-country pooled figure (1,970,012 / 25,125,597 = 7.84%), which is the sum of the four rows above; (b) the share of rated news outlets that are questionable (125/874 = 14.3% overall; France 49/236, Germany 25/221, Italy 29/204, UK 22/213) - this describes the composition of NewsGuard's rating list, not the prevalence of untrustworthy content; (c) the rho ratio of questionable to reliable retweets, which is the paper's main consumption measure but is reported only inside Fig 2 panels, with no numbers in the text; (d) the users' news-diet distribution (Fig 4, 'a small percentage predominantly consumes content from questionable sources'), whose numbers sit in Table S4 of the supplement, not in the text - this would have been the paper's EXPOSURE/diet estimate; (e) 'among the top 25 sources identified by the PageRank algorithm in each network, a substantial majority (at least 95.3%) are found to be reliable' - the misinformation share would be a complement I computed, which R8 forbids, and the set is rank-truncated; (f) the bot analysis (1.4% of high-similarity questionable-diet users flagged as bots), which is not a misinformation share. The topic-filtered dataset (Table 3, Brexit / Coronavirus / Covid Vaccine) gives user, source, tweet and retweet counts but no reliability split, so no per-topic prevalence can be computed from the text.

rob.design: Full census of tweets posted between 1 January 2019 and 11 November 2021 by all Twitter accounts of news outlets based in France, Germany, Italy and the UK that are rated by NewsGuard (874 outlets, 749 reliable and 125 questionable; 25,125,597 tweets). Reliability is assigned at outlet level by NewsGuard's nine-criterion trust score with a cut-off of 60, so there is no article-level verification and no inter-coder reliability. NewsGuard coverage is said to represent at least 90% of engagement per country. Topic selection used BERTopic plus keyword filters, validated against Google Trends. Only four countries were studied because NewsGuard ratings are unavailable elsewhere; single platform.
rob.item6_quote: News sources are categorized into two groups based on their score: Reliable (trust score greater or equal to 60) and Questionable (trust score less than 60).
